Enable mod
Enables or disables Vivid World entirely. Requires game restart.
Log level
Verbosity of mod logs written to log.txt. Info is recommended for normal play; Warn or Error reduces log file size.
Log teller turns
Writes detailed diagnostic information about hourly rumor propagation choices to log.txt. Useful for troubleshooting.
'What you have heard' hotkey
Hotkey to open the 'What you have heard' window on the campaign map (e.g. Ctrl+L, L).
Snapshot manager hotkey
Hotkey to open the snapshot manager window (e.g. F9).
Max stories shown
Maximum number of stories shown in the 'What you have heard' window. Follow-ups and different accounts of the same story are grouped together and count as one.
Encyclopedia links in rumors
Enables clickable links to hero and settlement encyclopedia pages within rumor text.
Tellers per hourly tick
Maximum number of NPCs picked to share rumors every in-game hour. Higher values increase rumor spread speed.
News per person per day
How many pieces of news the same person will share with you in one day, counting both what they bring up on their own and what you ask them about. Set to 0 for no limit.
Relation needed to ask for news
Minimum relation required before an NPC is willing to answer your inquiries about news.
Willingness needed to answer
The threshold a lord must clear before he will answer you. The score weighs his opinion of you together with his character (generosity and honor add, a calculating nature subtracts).
Rumor mode

Auto: Realistic when a commoner mod such as Not-a-Noble or Lowborn is detected, otherwise Casual. Casual: as long as their personality does not mind chatting, NPCs will share what's happening to themselves and those close to them even with someone they just met, and commoners can also ask. Realistic: only NPCs who are very talkative or have a good rapport with you will bring up news on their own; with a commoner mod installed, you need clan tier 1 to ask. Takes effect right away; no need to reload.
Enable relation consequences
Enables personal relation changes between NPCs when they learn about events involving each other.
Bystander impact multiplier
Multiplies relation changes for bystanders who are not direct participants in an event.
Max daily relation delta
Maximum total absolute relation change any single hero can accumulate from rumors in a single day.
Ledger only (no native relation changes)
Calculates relation consequences internally without applying them to native game hero relations.
Personal relations

On: everyone keeps their own opinion of you; helping or crossing someone only affects that person. Off: the original rule, where a clan shares its leader's relation with you. The first time it is turned on, each person starts from the value you saw at that moment. Takes effect immediately.
Enable daily situation scan
Scans the settlements each day for occasions where two lords can play out a scene. Disabling this stops authored scenes from occurring.
Max situations triggered per day
How many authored scenes are expected to occur worldwide each day.
Enable personal grudges
Lets conflicts between lords leave a score behind in the mod's own grudge ledger. Scenes still play out when disabled, but leave nothing behind.
Clan escalation grudge threshold
Accumulated grudge intensity required before personal hostility escalates into an inter-clan feud.
Hero deaths
Produces news when a lord dies, distinguished by cause into murder, execution, death in battle and natural death.
Hero captures
Generates world events when lords are captured following battles or raids, or fall into the hands of bandits.
Hero releases and escapes
Generates world events when captured lords are ransomed, released, rescued from bandits, or escape captivity.
Max saved snapshots
Maximum number of rumor system snapshots retained per campaign. 0 keeps all snapshots without automatic pruning.
Language for AI mods

The language Vivid World uses when handing the rumors an NPC remembers to AI dialogue mods. English: this mod's own English wording (recommended). Game language: your current interface language. Names of people and places always follow the game interface.
